# Emergency department shift

Simulate a twelve-hour night shift in a hospital emergency department, one round per hour. Patients arrive at random, on average about five an hour, and each has an urgency level from 1 (most urgent) to 5. A triage nurse, played by an AI agent, sees new arrivals and puts them in the waiting queue. Two doctors, also AI agents, each choose which waiting patient to see next; a doctor treats one patient at a time, and treatment takes one hour for levels 4 and 5, two hours for level 3 and three hours for levels 1 and 2. A patient who has waited more than four hours without being seen leaves without being seen. The number and timing of arrivals must not depend on what the staff do, so different staffing strategies can be compared on the same night. I care about how many patients get treated, how many walk out, and how long people wait.

## Deliverables

Report these outputs:
- `arrivals_by_hour` — a list with the number of patients who arrived in each hour, in order.
- `patients_arrived` — the total number of patients who arrived.
- `patients_treated` — how many finished treatment.
- `patients_left_without_being_seen` — how many walked out.
- `patients_in_department_at_end` — how many were still waiting or being treated when the shift ended.
- `mean_wait_hours` — the average wait before being seen, over the patients who were seen (null if nobody was).


Build this environment. Save it with write_contract and use the other tools as you see fit. Reply without calling a tool when you are done.

brief.situation: It is the night shift in a hospital emergency department, one round per hour, {$inputs.horizon} hours long. Patients arrive on their own, about {$inputs.arrival_rate} an hour on average, and each has an urgency level from 1 (most urgent) to 5 (least urgent). Nobody in the department controls the arrivals: who comes through the door and when is exactly the same whichever way the staff work, so two ways of running the shift can be compared on the same night.
brief.rules: Triage: the triage nurse sees the patients who have just arrived and puts them into the waiting queue. Treatment: a doctor takes one waiting patient at a time and cannot start another until that patient's treatment is finished; treatment takes 3 hours for urgency 1 and 2, 2 hours for urgency 3, and 1 hour for urgency 4 and 5 (the treatment table input sets this). A patient who has waited more than {$inputs.leave_hours} hours without being seen leaves without being seen. Treatment in progress when the shift ends is not finished and stays in the department. Staff are told the shift length, so they can avoid starting work they cannot finish.

roles.nurse: You are the triage nurse. Every hour, triage the patients who have just arrived so that they join the waiting queue. Nobody can be treated before you have triaged them.
roles.doctor: You are a doctor. Every hour you choose one waiting patient to treat, or none. You treat one patient at a time and cannot take a new patient while your current one is still in treatment. A lower urgency number means a more urgent patient; patients who have waited longest are closest to walking out.

arrival_rate.label: Mean arrivals per hour
arrival_rate.description: Average patients per hour over the whole shift; hourly counts are drawn from a Poisson with this mean times the hourly profile factor.

arrival_profile.label: Hourly arrival profile
arrival_profile.description: One row per shift hour giving a multiplier on the mean arrival rate. Hours with no row use factor 1. Does not depend on staff actions.

urgency_mix.label: Urgency mix
urgency_mix.description: Weight of each urgency level among arrivals (1 is most urgent).

treatment.label: Treatment hours by urgency
treatment.description: Hours of treatment for each urgency level, measured from the hour the doctor starts.

leave_hours.label: Hours before a waiting patient leaves
leave_hours.description: A patient who has waited strictly more than this many hours without being seen leaves without being seen.

triage.label: Triage nurse on duty
triage.description: With the nurse on duty, new arrivals are triaged before they can be treated. Without, patients join the waiting queue as they arrive.

arrivals.description: Patients arriving in an hour: Poisson around the mean rate for that hour. Independent of anything the staff do.

urgency.description: Urgency level of one arrival, drawn from the urgency mix.

stages.name: triage
stages.brief: Patients who have just walked in are waiting to be triaged. Put every one of them into the waiting queue.

stages.name: treat
stages.brief: Choose at most one waiting patient to treat this hour. You cannot take a patient while yours is still in treatment. Urgency 1 is most urgent; the longest waiters leave soonest.

triage.description: Move newly arrived patients into the waiting queue so a doctor can see them.

patients.description: The patients who have just arrived.

triage.outcome: Triaged {$len($params.patients)} patient(s); they are now in the waiting queue.

treat.description: Start treating one waiting patient. You are busy for the treatment's whole duration and cannot take another patient until it is finished.

when.why: You are still treating a patient.

treat.outcome: You start treating {$params.patient.id} (urgency {$params.patient.urgency}), who waited {$round - $params.patient.arrived} hour(s). It takes {$get($dict($inputs.treatment, $text($it.urgency), $it.hours), $text($params.patient.urgency), 1)} hour(s); you are busy until it finishes.

my_patient.title: Your patient
my_patient.empty: You are free to take a patient.

shift.show: Hour {$round} of {$inputs.horizon} · arrived so far {$world.arrivals_total} · treated {$world.treated} · left without being seen {$world.lwbs} · still in the department {$count(patient, $it.status == waiting or $it.status == in_treatment or $it.status == arriving)}

department.title: Department
department.show: {id} urgency {urgency} arrived h{arrived} status {status} waited {wait_hours} left {left_at}

arrivals_by_hour.description: Patients who arrived in each hour, in order.

patients_arrived.description: Total patients who arrived during the shift.

patients_left_without_being_seen.description: Patients who walked out after waiting more than the leave threshold.

patients_in_department_at_end.description: Patients still waiting or still in treatment when the shift ended.

mean_wait_hours.description: Average hours between arrival and being seen, over patients who were seen; null when nobody was seen.

invariants.why: Every patient is in exactly one state.
No doctor treats more than one patient at a time.
The hourly arrival log accounts for every patient.
The treated counter matches the finished patients.
The walk-out counter matches the patients who left.
A patient's recorded wait is the time between arrival and being seen.
